thread:
Maya (Support): Customer reporting a burst of 429s and occasional 401s when prefetching long contexts to rwd-pro-max-64k. Happens during heavy fanout (8x prefetches per user). Any quick triage ideas? :thinking_face:
Jasper (Infra): Do we have request IDs or example logs? 429s can be different classes: quota vs concurrency vs context rejection. 401s might be key/billing.
Maya (Support): Pasting sanitized request snippet and one request id we saw: 
```
POST /v1/generate
Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED
Model: rwd-pro-max-64k
Content-Length: 512000
X-Request-ID: rq_0bcd1234
Payload: {"context_tokens":80000,"prefetch_count":8} 
```
Jasper (Infra): Good, that payload helps. Are the 429s returning an error string like "over_concurrency" or "rate_limit"?
Maya (Support): Mostly just 429 with body: "error": "quota_exhausted" sometimes "error": "over_concurrency". 401s seen ~1% of calls, often right after a burst.
Luis (Runtime): Quick facts for rwd-pro-max-64k: per-api-key soft RPM=2800, hard RPM=3500, TPM=1400, max_concurrency=28, model-max-context=65536. If you exceed context limit we return immediate 400/422, but very large request bodies + many fanouts can hit concurrency accounting and per-key RPM.
Sana (Billing): The intermittent 401s sound like transient billing auth failure — sometimes the billing service throttles API keys with pending invoice checks. I checked the account: no hard suspension, but we flagged a billing anomaly at 2023-10-12T14:02UTC which coincides with the spike.
Maya (Support): Customer is on a committed plan, weirdly. They said their app does a prefetch across 8 subrequests per user on every page load.
Jasper (Infra): That pattern multiplies concurrency and RPM by fanout. Our edge queues count each prefetch as separate inflight request. If many users do this simultaneously, you can exceed per-key RPM and concurrency even if individual requests are within limits.
Jasper (Infra): I pulled trace rq_0bcd1234 -> backend shows spikes in active connections and a short auth retry loop right before the 401s. I opened a trace: tracebot: Created trace https://traces.internal/trace/rq_0bcd1234
Luis (Runtime): Mitigations: 1) Recommend client-side collapsing (single multi-turn request instead of 8 prefetches) or server-side batching. 2) Add jittered backoff + exponential retry on 429s. 3) For sustained throughput, upgrade to Dedicated or request a per-key concurrency/RPM exception.
Sana (Billing): As a short-term measure I applied a 30-minute soft quota bump to this tenant so they can recover while we investigate. I'll follow up if we need a longer increase.
Maya (Support): Added repro script for their devs to simulate the pattern:
```bash
for i in {1..50}; do \
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \ \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \ \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ \
    -d '{"model":"rwd-pro-max-64k","prompt":"...","prefetch_count":8}' &
done; wait
```
Maya (Support): Customer ran that and reproduced ~70% 429s within seconds. They accepted the temporary guidance.
Jasper (Infra): Follow-ups for infra: consider adding per-tenant elastic queueing to smooth fanout bursts and a more visible signal in the Console when prefetch patterns cause backpressure. Filed INF-4821 to track.
Sana (Billing): I'll coordinate a billing review to ensure the committed plan mapping is correct; if they keep this pattern we'll propose Dedicated or an enlarged rate package.
Maya (Support): Closing note — shared mitigation steps with customer: collapse prefetches, add retry with jitter, monitor for 401s and contact us if 401s persist. Reopen if they hit it again. :white_check_mark:
